title: Avoiding Instruction-Centric Microarchitectural Timing Channels Via Binary-Code Transformations
problem: Microarchitectural optimizations introduce instruction-centric timing side channels that cannot be mitigated at the source-code level. These channels leak information through timing variations correlated with instruction execution patterns on optimized microarchitectures.
motivation: As Moore's Law ends and microarchitectural optimizations accelerate, novel timing side channels pose growing security risks requiring practical mitigation techniques.
method: The approach applies binary-code transformations to eliminate instruction-centric timing channels. By modifying binary code rather than source, the technique disrupts timing-sensitive instruction sequences and removes correlations between observable timing and sensitive computations.
key_novelty: First to propose binary-level code transformations as a generic mitigation for instruction-centric microarchitectural timing channels that inherently cannot be fixed at the source-code level.
contributions: Characterizes how microarchitectural optimizations enable instruction-centric timing side channels
Develops binary-code transformation techniques to eliminate these timing channels
Demonstrates that timing side-channel mitigation requires binary-level intervention beyond source-code defenses

metrics.other: Timing channel leakage reduction, performance overhead of binary transformations

limitations: Not discussed in the provided abstract.
